text:
MIN arrives on a five-game road trip (0-1-1 so far) after a 2-1 loss at CGY two days ago, and is 2-2-1 in its last five without Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno. SEA is 3-1-1 in its last five after beating UTA 5-3, missing Jacob Melanson and Ryan Lindgren. The story is results against chances. The Kraken's goal difference runs ahead of their chances, with finishing doing the lifting, while the Wild have had more of the play (54% of the expected goals at five on five, which measures chance quality, against 45% for SEA) and not enough to show for it.

MIN's power play is the stronger unit (0.84 expected goals per game to 0.63), and it has also been better at killing penalties (0.82 allowed to 0.66 for SEA, where lower is better). In net, projected starters Jesper Wallstedt (+6.8 goals saved above expected this season) and Philipp Grubauer (+3.3) both rate well, with Wallstedt ahead. Our model has MIN at 3.27 expected goals tonight and SEA at 2.70.

For players to watch, Kirill Kaprizov is 51% to score and 79% for a point, and Matt Boldy is 46% and 69%. Quinn Hughes is two points from 500 career points. Our under-the-radar pick is Joel Eriksson Ek, 58% for a point, above his season pace because his line creates chances. For SEA, Jared McCann (28% to score) leads the power play. Frederick Gaudreau has 7 points in his last ten against his former team, though finishing is driving most of that.
